title: The shift register that is not a shift register

prereqs.why: The entire question is what = does in a clocked block that <= would not.
The answer is about how many flip-flops the synthesiser infers, so you need to know what a flip-flop is for.

hints: `=` is a blocking assignment: it takes effect immediately, and the next statement in the block sees the new value. Trace what `q2 = q1` reads.
Ask yourself how many distinct values can exist in this block at the end of one clock edge.
The fix is one character per line, and it is the difference between describing hardware and describing a sequence of steps.

options: All three registers load `d` on the same clock edge, so `q1`, `q2` and `q3` are always equal — one stage of delay in total, not three.
Exactly what was intended: three flip-flops in series, giving three cycles of delay.
A combinational path from `d` to `q3` with no flip-flops at all, because blocking assignments never infer registers.
Three flip-flops, but with the stages in reverse order, so `d` appears at `q3` first and `q1` last.
